content: 1. The drug elbasvir/grazoprevir can affect the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored, and the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates should be adjusted if clinically indicated. 2. Elbasvir/grazoprevir increases the levels of seladelpar through mechanisms involving other pathways. Caution is advised, and seladelpar should be monitored for adverse effects when co-administered with BCRP inhibitors. 3. Elbasvir/grazoprevir increases the levels of simvastatin through an unknown mechanism. If co-administered, the lowest necessary dose of simvastatin should be used, and therapy should be closely monitored. 4. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir increases the levels of elbasvir/grazoprevir through inhibition of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, and OATP2B1 transporters. Caution is advised, and therapy should be closely monitored. 5. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of reduced therapeutic efficacy. 6. Strong CYP3A inducers reduce the therapeutic effect of elbasvir/grazoprevir and are contraindicated. Therapy should be closely monitored. 7. Stiripentol, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, affects the metabolism of elbasvir/grazoprevir. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored, and CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol should be monitored for increased or decreased effects. Dosage adjustments may be required. 8. Elbasvir/grazoprevir increases tacrolimus levels through an unknown mechanism. Tacrolimus whole blood concentrations, renal function, and associated adverse events should be frequently monitored if co-administered. 9. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and therapy should be closely monitored. 10. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by weakly inducing CYP3A4. Sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be monitored for effectiveness if co-administered. 11. Tipranavir increases the levels of elbasvir/grazoprevir through other mechanisms. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of serious adverse effects. Alternative therapies should be used. 12. Trofinetide, an OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 inhibitor, increases plasma levels of OATP1B1 or OATP1B3 substrates. Co-administration with sensitive substrates should be avoided, and alternative drugs should be considered. 13. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A substrates should be avoided, especially when minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. If unavoidable, the CYP3A substrate dose should be reduced according to product labeling. 14. Voclosporin, an OATP1B1 inhibitor, may increase the concentration of OATP1B1 substrates. Adverse reactions of OATP1B1 substrates should be monitored when co-administered with voclosporin. 15. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and therapy should be closely monitored. 16. Patients should be tested for current or prior hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection before initiating treatment with hepatitis C virus (HCV) direct-acting antivirals (DAAs). HBV reactivation has been reported in HCV/HBV co-infected patients undergoing or completing DAA treatment without HBV antiviral therapy. Some cases have resulted in fulminant hepatitis, hepatic failure, and death. 17. HCV/HBV co-infected patients should be monitored for hepatitis flare or HBV reactivation during HCV treatment and post-treatment follow-up. Appropriate management for HBV infection should be initiated as clinically indicated. 18. Patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B or C) or a history of hepatic decompensation are at risk of hepatic decompensation. Therapy should be discontinued in patients who develop evidence of hepatic decompensation or failure. 19. If administered with ribavirin, the contraindications for ribavirin also apply to this combination regimen. Refer to ribavirin prescribing information for details. 20. HBV reactivation is characterized by an abrupt increase in HBV replication, manifesting as a rapid increase in serum HBV DNA levels. Monitor liver enzymes prior to therapy, at treatment week 8, and as clinically indicated. For patients receiving 16 weeks of therapy, additional hepatic laboratory testing should be performed at treatment week 12. 21. Postmarketing cases of hepatic decompensation or failure, including fatal outcomes, have been reported. Patients with compensated cirrhosis (Child-Pugh A) or advanced liver disease (e.g., portal hypertension) may require more frequent hepatic laboratory testing. Monitor for signs and symptoms of hepatic decompensation, such as jaundice, ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, and variceal hemorrhage. 22. Warnings and precautions for ribavirin, including pregnancy-related risks, apply if co-administered. Ribavirin is contraindicated in pregnant women and men whose female partners are pregnant. 23. There is no adequate human data on the use of elbasvir or grazoprevir during pregnancy. Animal studies have shown no evidence of adverse developmental outcomes at exposures greater than those in humans at the recommended dose. 24. It is unknown if elbasvir or grazoprevir is distributed in human breast milk. Consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding, the mother’s clinical need for the drug, and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed infant. 25. Elbasvir and grazoprevir are partially eliminated by oxidative metabolism, primarily via CYP3A. No circulating metabolites of either drug were detected in human plasma. Excretion occurs predominantly through feces (>90%) and minimally through urine (<1%). The half-life is 24 hours for elbasvir and 31 hours for grazoprevir. 26. Population pharmacokinetic analyses estimate that elbasvir and grazoprevir AUCs are 15% and 50% higher, respectively, in Asians compared to Caucasians. 27. Elbasvir and grazoprevir may be taken with or without food. Store at 20–25°C (68–77°F), with excursions permitted between 15–30°C (59–86°F).
